stem: Under Article XIII of the 1987 Constitution, who may provide for other cases of human rights violations to fall within the authority of the Commission on Human Rights (CHR)?
choices: Congress, taking into account the CHR's recommendations
The CHR alone, by adopting its own rules of procedure
The President, through an executive order on human rights
The Supreme Court, through its rulings on human rights cases
answer: Congress, taking into account the CHR's recommendations
hints: Section 18 lists what the CHR can do now. The question asks who can add more. Look at the next section, Section 19.
Section 19 names one body that "may provide for other cases", and gives the CHR a smaller role.
In Section 19 the CHR only gives recommendations, so it is not the one that decides. Of the rest, pick the body that Section 19 names.

solution.methodName: Recall the exact words of the provision

steps.action: Find the provision: Article XIII, Section 19 of the 1987 Constitution.
Read it: "The Congress may provide for other cases of violations of human rights that should fall within the authority of the Commission, taking into account its recommendations."
So Congress decides, and the CHR's part is to give recommendations.
steps.why: "Its recommendations" means the CHR's recommendations. Congress must take them into account.

steps.action: The CHR's own rules of procedure (Section 18) govern how it works. They do not add new kinds of cases.
Section 19 does not mention the President or the Supreme Court.
The answer is Congress, taking into account the CHR's recommendations.

trapNotes.The CHR alone, by adopting its own rules: Section 18 lets the CHR adopt its own rules of procedure, but Section 19 gives the power to add new cases to Congress. The CHR only recommends.
trapNotes.The President, through an executive orde: Section 19 does not mention the President. It names Congress.
